questions.q: Fill up per p109: Primary Angle Closure Glaucoma is AKA ___.
questions.exp: AKA Acute Congestive Glaucoma; m/c age 60-70 yrs. (Book p109)

questions.q: PACG is m/c at age per p109:
questions.exp: m/c age 60-70 yrs. (Book p109)

questions.q: Correct sequential mechanism of PACG per p109:
opts: Iris bombe → relative pupillary block → PAS → ITC
PAS → ITC → iris bombe → relative pupillary block
Relative pupillary block → iris bombe → ITC → PAS
ITC → relative pupillary block → iris bombe → PAS
questions.exp: Relative pupillary block → iris bombe (anterior bowing of iris) → irido trabecular contact (ITC) → if persistent, peripheral anterior synechiae (PAS). (Book p109)

questions.q: In relative pupillary block per p109, aqueous cannot flow from ___ and the pushing effect is d/t ↑ pressure in ___.
opts: TM to Schlemm canal; episcleral veins
questions.exp: Apposition of pupillary margin against lens surface → aqueous cannot flow from PC → AC → pushing effect d/t ↑ pressure in PC. (Book p109)

questions.q: Which statement on PACG mechanism per p109 is TRUE?
opts: PAS is iris adhesion with cornea and trabecular meshwork disrupting inflow from PC to AC
Iris bombe means posterior bowing of iris
Relative pupillary block apposes pupillary margin against cornea
questions.exp: PAS = iris adhesion with cornea and trabecular meshwork → disruption of inflow from PC to AC; iris bombe = ANTERIOR bowing of iris; pupillary block = apposition of pupillary margin against LENS surface. (Book p109)

questions.q: All increase the chance of iris opposing cornea (PACG risk factors) per p109 EXCEPT:
opts: Small cornea with ↓ radius and ↑ curvature
questions.exp: Risk factors d/t ↑ chance of iris opposing cornea: shallow AC, hypermetropia (small AC), females (smaller AC), plateau iris, small cornea (↓ radius with ↑ curvature). (Book p109)

questions.q: A 65-year-old lady develops severe ocular pain after a movie in a dim theatre. Per p109 the precipitating sequence is:
opts: Dim light → pupil constriction → angle widens
Dim light → pupil dilation → iris moves towards angle → angle closure
questions.exp: Precipitated by dim light (eg movie theatre) → dilation of pupil → iris moves towards angle → angle closure. (Book p109)

questions.q: Match ACG classification per p109 — 1) PACS 2) PAC 3) PACG … A) Raised IOP with abnormal OD and VF, ITC ≥3 quadrants with PAS, definitive Rx B) Normal IOP/OD/VF, ITC ≥3 quadrants, prophylactic Rx C) Raised IOP with normal OD and VF, ITC ≥3 quadrants with PAS, definitive Rx
questions.exp: PACS normal IOP/OD/VF with ITC ≥3 quadrants → prophylactic; PAC raised IOP with normal OD/VF + PAS → definitive; PACG raised IOP with abnormal OD/VF + PAS → definitive. PACS 1° angle closure suspect; PAC 1° angle closure; PACG 1° angle closure glaucoma. (Book p109)

questions.q: All are acute symptoms of PACG per p110 EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Symptoms present acutely: diminution of vision, redness, severe pain, headache, vomiting, coloured halos around lights. (Book p110)

questions.q: IOP in acute PACG per p110 is typically:
questions.exp: IOP >40 mmHg → severe pain; digital tonometry: rock hard eye. (Book p110)

questions.q: Digital tonometry in acute PACG per p110 feels like:
questions.exp: Digital tonometry: rock hard eye. (Book p110)

questions.q: On torchlight in PACG per p110 one sees:
questions.exp: On torchlight: eclipse sign (shallow AC). (Book p110)

questions.q: Hazy cornea/corneal edema of PACG per p110 is d/t:
opts: Breakage of tight junctions b/w endothelial cells by ↑ IOP → corneal decompensation
questions.exp: Hazy cornea/corneal edema: breakage of tight junctions b/w endothelial cells by ↑ IOP → corneal decompensation. (Book p110)

questions.q: Coloured haloes around lights in PACG per p110 occur d/t:
opts: Prismatic dispersion of light rays by corneal edema
questions.exp: Hazy cornea leads to diminution of vision and coloured haloes around light d/t prismatic dispersion of light rays. (Book p110)

questions.q: Match Vogt's triad per p110 — 1) Iris atrophy 2) Posterior synechiae 3) Glaukomflecken … A) Anterior capsular/subcapsular opacities d/t epithelial ischemia and necrosis (2° to ↑ IOP) B) D/t ↑ pressure → ischemia C) Adhesion b/w pupillary margin and anterior surface of lens
questions.exp: Vogt's triad: iris atrophy (d/t ↑ pressure → ischemia), posterior synechiae (adhesion b/w pupillary margin and anterior surface of lens), glaukomflecken cataract (anterior capsular/subcapsular opacities d/t epithelial ischemia and necrosis, 2° to ↑ IOP). (Book p110)

questions.q: Vertically oval pupil in the acute attack per p111 is d/t:
opts: Iris atrophy preferentially superior and inferior
questions.exp: Vertically oval d/t iris atrophy (preferentially superior and inferior atrophy). (Book p111)

questions.q: Which statement on the pupil per p111 is TRUE?
opts: Mid dilated d/t sphincter atrophy; fixed d/t posterior synechiae effects
The fixed pupil still constricts briskly to light once IOP is controlled
Mid dilation is due to dilator pupillae hypertrophy
The pupil remains small and reacts normally
questions.exp: Mid dilated d/t atrophy of sphincter pupillae; fixed = neither constricting nor dilating, d/t posterior synechiae effects. (Book p111)

questions.q: Match per p111 — 1) Acute VF change 2) Chronic VF change 3) Optic disc … A) Central nasal step B) Superior field constriction C) Same as POAG but often not visualized d/t hazy cornea
questions.exp: Visual field changes: acute → superior field constriction; chronic → central nasal step. Optic disc: same as in POAG; not visualized d/t anterior chamber changes (hazy cornea). (Book p111)

questions.q: Optic disc assessment in acute PACG per p111:
opts: Always shows florid disc neovascularization in every case
Shows a cherry-red spot at the macula
Not visualized d/t hazy cornea; when seen same as POAG
questions.exp: Optic disc changes: same as in POAG; not visualized d/t anterior chamber changes (hazy cornea). (Book p111)

questions.q: First step of acute PACG mx per p111 (treated as ocular emergency):
opts: ↓ IOP: IV mannitol or tab acetazolamide or oral glycerin
questions.exp: Step 1: ↓ IOP with IV mannitol (2.5%) or tab acetazolamide 250 mg 2 tablets stat or oral glycerin 1 g/kg. (Book p111)

questions.q: IV mannitol regimen per p111:
questions.exp: IV Mannitol (2.5%): 1.2 g/min over 30 min; DOC for acute episode/exacerbations; cannot be given long term d/t diuretic effect. (Book p111)

questions.q: Per p111: Tab acetazolamide 250 mg stat = ___ tablets; oral glycerin dose = ___ g/kg of body weight.
questions.exp: Tab Acetazolamide 250 mg → 2 tablets stat; oral glycerin 1 g/kg of body weight. (Book p111)

questions.q: Which statement on pilocarpine in the acute attack per p111 is TRUE?
opts: It works best while IOP is still maximal
It is the drug that lowers IOP fastest
It is ineffective before IOP normalises d/t inability to constrict if ↑ IOP
questions.exp: Step 2 miosis: DOC pilocarpine (constricts pupil) but ineffective before IOP normalises (d/t inability to constrict if ↑ IOP). (Book p111)

questions.q: Ocular side effects of pilocarpine per p111 include all EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Ocular side effects: transient myopia, punctal occlusion, uveitis. Eyelid retraction is an α-agonist effect (Book p106), not pilocarpine. (Book p111)

questions.q: Pilocarpine cannot be given long term per p111 d/t:
questions.exp: Cannot be given long term d/t miosis: impaired dark adaptation. (Book p111)

questions.q: Per p111 note, while using timolol one should advise:
questions.exp: Note: Timolol → nasolacrimal duct occlusion. (Book p111)

questions.q: After steps 1 and 2, cornea clear (most cases) per p111. Next:
questions.exp: Step 3 assess corneal clarity: clear (most cases) → plan for Sx; hazy (rare) → repeat step 1 and 2. (Book p111)

questions.q: After acute Rx the cornea remains hazy (rare) per p111. Next best step:
questions.exp: Hazy (rare): repeat step 1 and 2. (Book p111)

questions.q: Definitive mx of PACG per p112:
opts: Laser iridotomy preferred; TOC for PACG and prophylaxis
Open iridectomy is always performed first in every patient
Long term pilocarpine as definitive therapy
Trabeculectomy is needed in every case
questions.exp: Laser iridotomy: preferred over open iridectomy; TOC for PACG and prophylaxis of PACG. (Book p112)

questions.q: Laser iridotomy photodisruption per p112 uses:
questions.exp: Photodisruption with Nd:YAG laser: 1064 nm; creation of hole in iris b/w 11 o'clock to 1 o'clock. (Book p112)

questions.q: Iridotomy hole is created b/w ___ so that it is covered by the upper eyelid (p112).
questions.exp: Creation of hole in iris b/w 11 o'clock to 1 o'clock; iridotomy hole at 11 o'clock covered by upper eyelid. (Book p112)

questions.q: Monocular diplopia after iridotomy per p112 occurs when:
opts: A single superior hole is covered by lid
2 sets of light rays enter the eye (eg holes at 11 and 6 o'clock)
questions.exp: Iridotomy holes at 11 and 6 o'clock → 2 sets of light rays enter eye → monocular diplopia; iridectomy b/w 11-10 o'clock keeps superior iris covered by eyelid → diplopia prevented. (Book p112)

questions.q: Match per p112 — 1) Laser iridotomy 2) Iridectomy b/w 11-10 o'clock 3) Diode cyclophotocoagulation … A) Superior iris covered by eyelid → diplopia prevented; aqueous inflow enabled → IOP and iris bombe resolve B) Nd:YAG 1064 nm photodisruption; TOC for PACG and prophylaxis C) 810 nm for painful blind absolute glaucoma → pain relief
questions.exp: Laser iridotomy Nd:YAG TOC/prophylaxis; iridectomy superiorly covered by eyelid prevents diplopia and enables aqueous inflow → IOP and iris bombe resolve; diode 810 nm cyclophotocoagulation relieves pain in absolute glaucoma. (Book p112)

questions.q: A blind, severely painful absolute glaucoma eye per p112. Best Rx:
opts: Latanoprost eye drops once daily at night
Diode laser (810 nm) cyclophotocoagulation for pain relief
Pilocarpine 2% drops four times a day
questions.exp: Rx of absolute glaucoma: no vision (blind); severe pain → diode laser (810 nm) cyclophotocoagulation → enables pain relief. (Book p112)

questions.q: Post Sx mild ↑ IOP of 21-22 mmHg per p112 is managed with:
questions.exp: Post Sx management: if mild ↑ IOP present (21-22 mmHg) → latanoprost. (Book p112)

units.title: Overview, mechanism, risk factors and PACS/PAC/PACG classification
units.guide: AKA Acute Congestive Glaucoma m/c age 60-70 yrs Mechanism a Relative pupillary block apposition of pupillary margin against lens surface aqueous cannot flow PC→AC pushing effect d/t ↑ pressure in PC b Iris bombe anterior bowing of iris c Irido trabecular contact (ITC) if persistent d Peripheral anterior synechiae (PAS) iris adhesion with cornea and trabecular meshwork disruption of inflow PC to AC Risk factors d/t ↑ chance iris opposing cornea shallow AC hypermetropia small AC females smaller AC plateau iris small cornea ↓ radius ↑ curvature Precipitated by dim light eg movie theatre → dilation of pupil → iris moves towards angle → angle closure Convexity of slit d/t iris convexity Classification PACS normal IOP/OD/VF ITC ≥3 quadrants prophylactic PAC raised IOP normal OD/VF ≥3 quadrants + PAS definitive PACG raised IOP abnormal OD/VF ≥3 quadrants + PAS definitive PACS 1° angle closure suspect PAC 1° angle closure PACG 1° angle closure glaucoma.

units.title: Manifestations — symptoms, IOP, eclipse sign, hazy cornea, Vogt's triad
units.guide: Symptoms present acutely diminution of vision redness severe pain headache vomiting coloured halos around lights Signs seen acutely IOP >40 mmHg severe pain digital tonometry rock hard eye On torchlight eclipse sign (shallow AC) Slit lamp 1 congestion/hyperemia 2 hazy cornea/corneal edema breakage of tight junctions b/w endothelial cells by ↑ IOP → corneal decompensation leads to diminution of vision and coloured haloes d/t prismatic dispersion of light rays 3 Vogt's triad iris atrophy (d/t ↑ pressure → ischemia) posterior synechiae adhesion b/w pupillary margin and anterior surface of lens glaukomflecken cataract anterior capsular/subcapsular opacities d/t epithelial ischemia and necrosis (2° to ↑ IOP).

units.title: Pupil, fields, disc; acute mx steps 1-2 (mannitol, acetazolamide, glycerin, pilocarpine)
units.guide: 4 Pupillary findings vertically oval d/t iris atrophy (preferentially superior and inferior) mid dilated d/t atrophy of sphincter pupillae fixed neither constricting nor dilating d/t posterior synechiae effects 5 Visual field changes acute superior field constriction chronic central nasal step 6 Optic disc same as POAG not visualized d/t anterior chamber changes (hazy cornea) Treatment ocular emergency ACUTE Mx Step 1 ↓ IOP a IV mannitol (2.5%) 1.2 g/min over 30 min DOC acute episode/exacerbations cannot long term d/t diuretic effect or b Tab acetazolamide 250 mg 2 tablets stat or c Oral glycerin 1 g/kg Step 2 miosis DOC pilocarpine ineffective before IOP normalises ocular side transient myopia punctal occlusion uveitis cannot long term d/t miosis impaired dark adaptation Note timolol → nasolacrimal duct occlusion.

units.title: Step 3 corneal clarity; definitive laser iridotomy (Nd:YAG 1064 nm)
units.guide: Step 3 assess corneal clarity clear (most cases) plan for Sx hazy (rare) repeat step 1 and 2 DEFINITIVE Mx Laser iridotomy preferred over open iridectomy TOC for PACG and prophylaxis of PACG Procedure photodisruption with Nd:YAG 1064 nm creation of hole in iris b/w 11 o'clock to 1 o'clock covered by upper eyelid.

units.title: Iridectomy positioning and diplopia, absolute glaucoma, post-Sx care
units.guide: Iridotomy holes at 11 and 6 o'clock → 2 sets of light rays enter eye → monocular diplopia Iridectomy b/w 11-10 o'clock superior iris covered by eyelid diplopia prevented aqueous inflow enabled IOP resolves iris bombe resolves Rx of absolute glaucoma no vision (blind) severe pain → diode laser (810 nm) cyclophotocoagulation → enables pain relief Post Sx management if mild ↑ IOP present (21-22 mmHg) → latanoprost.
